headline: Andy Taylor of Duran Duran died at 65. He started at 13.
summary: Andy Taylor, Duran Duran's guitarist, died at home on Monday at 65 after years with prostate cancer. A fisherman's son from Tynemouth, he taught himself guitar and was paid to play at 13. He answered an ad for a 'live-wire guitarist' in 1980 and co-wrote Rio and Girls on Film. He quit after Live Aid in 1985 and came back for one album.

cover_question.q: Why quit a band that famous?

cover_answer: They had stopped talking. Fame didn't fix that.
table_question: Would you stay on a winning team if nobody on it was talking?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: A man named Andy Taylor, who played guitar in a famous band, died. He was 65 and had been sick for a long time. He learned guitar by himself as a boy and got paid to play when he was 13, not much older than the big kids at school. His family was all around him at home, the way yours is around this table.
5-7.why: Sick a long time, old, and his family there: the three facts that keep a stranger's death from landing on their own. The guitar at 13 gives them something to hold instead.
5-7.why_long: A five-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, and here that is 'died'. So the script surrounds it: he was old, he was sick a long time, his family was with him at home. Cantor found the fear at this age is concrete and personal, so the last line puts them at their own table. Expect 'will you die?' Not for a long time.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: A fisherman's son answered an ad for a 'live-wire guitarist' and joined Duran Duran in 1980. MTV had just started, and their videos made them huge. At Live Aid in 1985 they had nothing to say to each other, he wrote, so he quit. Like a star leaving a winning team because the locker room went quiet.
8-12.why: A chain they can follow, and a score that came apart from the friendship.
8-12.why_long: A child this age is working out cause and effect. The chain is complete: an ad, a band, MTV, fame, then a bus to Live Aid where nobody spoke, and he quit. The locker-room line works on a child who keeps score: here the score and the friendship came apart. Expect 'did they make up?' Yes. He came back for one album in 2004.

13-17.script: Is a band a job or a friendship? Andy Taylor quit Duran Duran in 1985 because, he wrote, they had nothing to say to each other. Second: in 2022 a letter read at the Rock Hall said he had stage 4 cancer. He made one more record with them. What do you do with time you know is short?
13-17.why: He left them, then came back near the end. Is that a contradiction?
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: he walked out on the band, and he spent some of his last years making a record with the same men. The script asks whether a band is a job or a friendship, then what you do with time you know is short. Expect 'did he regret quitting?' In 2008 he said he always wanted to be in the band.

5-7.a: Everyone does, someday, and for me that's a long, long time away. He was 65 and sick for years.

8-12.q: Why quit a band that famous?
8-12.a: After Live Aid in 1985, he wrote, they had nothing to say to each other.
Yes. He came back for one album in 2004, and one more in 2023.

13-17.q: Why tell everyone he was dying?
13-17.a: He was too ill for the Rock Hall in 2022. A bandmate read his letter.
No. The singer and bassist were the pinups. He co-wrote the hits.
